documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, he's in his apartment, identity verified.

Smoking check-in as planned. Still about 10 cigarettes a day. Uses the gum a few times a week, mainly long days in the lab. Says winter break made it worse, more downtime. Thought about quitting over the holidays but didn't set anything.

No chest pain, no shortness of breath, no cough.

We talked through what a quit attempt could look like: pick a day after midterms, gum on a schedule rather than only when desperate, tell his roommates. He'll think about a date. Gum refills are on file.

A/P: Nicotine dependence, cigarettes, contemplative. Continue gum 2 mg PRN. Recheck at his physical in late summer, sooner if he wants help with a quit date.

documents.title: Was in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted to let you know my right lung collapsed again on Thursday. I was walking fast to class and it hit all at once. They did the needle and a chest tube again and kept me until Sunday. I'm home and feel ok, a bit sore. They said to see my primary doctor in a week or so.

documents.title: RE: Was in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry to hear it, Silas, glad you're home. Front desk will reach out to get you in next week. Any new chest pain or trouble breathing, go straight back to the ED. We'll ask the hospital to send their notes.

conditions.label: Spontaneous tension pneumothorax
conditions.note: right; ED needle decompression and chest tube, admitted 4/24-4/27

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-hospital visit. No records from the hospital yet; history is from him.

On 4/24 he was walking quickly to a class when he got sudden sharp pain on the right side of his chest and couldn't catch his breath. Taken to the ED. He was told his lung was fully down and pushing on the middle of his chest, so they put a needle in first and then a chest tube. Admitted, tube came out on day 3, discharged Sunday 4/27. Second right-sided collapse; first was 2022.

Since home: soreness at the tube site, improving, using nothing for it now. Breathing back to his normal. Walks to campus without trouble. No fever, no cough.

Still smoking, about half a pack. He knows. Says the hospital told him the same thing.

Exam: vitals as charted. Comfortable, speaking full sentences. Trachea midline. Lungs clear with equal breath sounds both sides, resonant. Right lateral tube site healing, clean and dry, no redness. Heart regular.

A/P:
1. Right tension pneumothorax 4/24/25, second right-sided episode. Clinically resolved. Added to problem list. Requested ED and inpatient records again. Reviewed: return to ED for any sudden chest pain or breathlessness; no flying until the hospital team clears him.
2. Nicotine dependence, cigarettes. Strongly advised stopping; each cigarette makes another collapse more likely. Still not ready to set a date. Continue nicotine gum.

RTC late August for his physical.

documents.title: Outside Emergency Department Record (April 24, 2025)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Received from the hospital emergency department by fax, second request. Date of service 04/24/2025.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PROVIDER NOTE

CC: right-sided chest pain, dyspnea.

HPI: 24M, graduate student, with a prior right spontaneous pneumothorax, brought in after abrupt sharp right chest pain and breathlessness that came on as he hurried to class this morning. Pain is worse with each breath in and did not ease when he stopped walking. Denies trauma.

PMH: right spontaneous pneumothorax 2022. Nicotine dependence.
PSH: right needle decompression and right chest tube (2022).
Meds: nicotine gum 2 mg PRN cravings.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father with repeated spontaneous pneumothoraces; paternal grandmother with Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome.
SH: smokes 1/2 ppd for 6 years. Alcohol 1-2 drinks per month. Graduate student.

Triage vitals: T 98.7 F, HR 112, RR 26, BP 102/66, SpO2 91% RA.

Exam: tall, thin young man, anxious, visibly dyspneic. No breath sounds on the right; right hemithorax hyperresonant. Trachea deviated to the left. Left lung clear. Tachycardic, regular.

MDM: presentation consistent with right tension pneumothorax. Portable chest film: large right pneumothorax with the mediastinum shifted to the left. Needle decompression, right 2nd intercostal space midclavicular line, with a rush of air and prompt improvement. Right chest tube placed under local anesthesia, 5th intercostal space anterior axillary line, without complication. Repeat film: tube in good position, lung re-expanded. CBC and BMP unremarkable.

Dx: right tension pneumothorax.
Dispo: admitted to the general surgery service.

----

DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 04/24/2025  Discharge 04/27/2025
Diagnosis: right tension pneumothorax, recurrent right-sided.
Course: chest tube to suction then water seal; air leak stopped on hospital day 2. Tube removed 04/26. Upright PA and lateral film 04/27: lung fully expanded, no residual pneumothorax. Ambulating, comfortable.
Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge meds: nicotine polacrilex gum 2 mg as needed.
Instructions: smoking cessation; no air travel for at least 2 weeks and until cleared; return for chest pain or shortness of breath. Follow up with PCP in 1 week.

--
Scanned. Reviewed by PCP; consistent with what he reported on 5/6.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

24 y/o here for yearly exam before fall semester starts.

Interval: right tension pneumothorax in April, hospital records now received and reviewed. No breathing trouble since. Back to walking everywhere. No chest pain, no cough, no wheeze.

Smoking: still 1/2 ppd, about 6 years now. Gum maybe twice a week. He says the April scare made him cut down for a few weeks and then it crept back. Still won't commit to a date; would rather try on his own first.

Alcohol: unchanged, a couple of drinks a month. No drugs. Sleep ok. Mood good; PHQ-9 2.

Meds: nicotine gum 2 mg PRN. Allergies: NKDA.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: vitals as charted. Tall, thin, well appearing. HEENT normal, dentition fine. Neck no adenopathy, thyroid normal, trachea midline. Lungs clear and equal bilaterally. Old tube scars right lateral chest, well healed. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly. Genitourinary deferred by patient. Skin no concerning lesions. Extremities normal. Neuro grossly intact.

A/P:
1. Preventive: CBC and CMP today. HIV and hep C already screened last year. Lipids done last year, normal; not repeating. Flu vaccine not in yet, he'll get one this fall.
2. Nicotine dependence, cigarettes: advised to quit again, gum continued, offered to set a date any time by message.
3. History of spontaneous pneumothorax, now two right-sided episodes including tension pneumothorax in April. Same ED precautions.

Return in a year.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Silas, Friday's blood counts and chemistry panel are all in the normal range. Good luck with the semester.

documents.title: Lung again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: It happened again on the 1st, same side. Worse than April, I could barely breathe. Needle and chest tube again and I was in until Wednesday. I'm ok now. Should I come in? Finals start soon so it would have to be after the semester if that's alright.

documents.title: RE: Lung again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know, and I'm sorry you went through that again. Yes, I'd like to see you. After finals is fine as long as you're breathing normally; if anything changes before then, ED right away. I'll ask the hospital for the records from this stay. Front desk can book you for January.

documents.title: RE: Lung again
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Silas, our January schedule opens next week. Reply here or call when you know your exam dates and we'll find a time.

documents.title: Outside Emergency Department Record (November 1, 2025)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Received from the hospital emergency department. Date of service 11/01/2025. Discharge summary for the inpatient stay not included; re-requested.

ED PROVIDER NOTE

CC: acute right chest pain, severe dyspnea.

HPI: 24-year-old man known to us from an April visit for right pneumothorax, now about 6 months later with sudden sharp right-sided chest pain and marked breathlessness that started while walking. No injury. No recent illness or fever.

PMH: right spontaneous pneumothorax 2022; right tension pneumothorax 04/2025. Nicotine dependence.
PSH: right needle decompression and chest tube (prior episodes).
Meds: nicotine gum 2 mg PRN.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father, recurrent spontaneous pneumothorax. Paternal grandmother, Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome.
SH: current smoker, 1/2 ppd x 6 years. 1-2 drinks/month. Graduate student.

Vitals on arrival: BP 92/58, HR 122, RR 28, SpO2 86% RA.

Exam: distressed. JVD present. Right hemithorax hyperresonant, breath sounds markedly reduced on the right, tactile fremitus decreased on the right. Left side clear to auscultation.

MDM: tension physiology. Portable film: large right pneumothorax, mediastinum shifted left. Immediate needle decompression right 2nd ICS MCL with improvement in pressure and saturation, then right chest tube 5th ICS AAL. Post-procedure film: right lung re-expanded, mediastinum midline. CBC, BMP within normal range.

Dx: recurrent right tension pneumothorax.
Dispo: admit to general surgery.

--
